title: Component styles come from a local CSS Module
intent: Paint follows the palette and a stylesheet reaches only what its component owns. A global stylesheet, a library's included, paints outside the palettes and reaches every element on the page, so only the bootstrap imports global ones, and only the token pipeline's three. A component may statically default-import its sibling Name.module.css, whose rules select its own classes, named as script identifiers, group them in @media, @container or @supports, and set layout and typography properties and paint. Paint takes a palette role: an ink for color, a surface for a background (one of the three the framework sets its own components on), a border token for a border, chosen so that every admitted ink over every admitted surface is a text pair the palette declares and holds to AA in every theme. A list marker takes a keyword, never copy. The import opt-out covers the import's form only: a finding inside the module names its CSS line and survives a marker on the import. Global selectors, imports, cross-file composition and a stylesheet loaded through import() or import.meta.glob are refused.

runtime.rationale: A stylesheet import is a build-graph edge; the bundler compiles it into the emitted CSS, after which module authorship does not exist.

reference: A component's own layout: import styles from "./Board.module.css", one static default binding, beside the component, with className={styles.board} on a native element. Ink: var(--color-fg-default), var(--color-fg-muted), var(--color-fg-subtle). Surfaces: var(--color-bg-canvas), var(--color-bg-surface), var(--color-bg-subtle). Borders: var(--color-border-default), var(--color-border-strong), var(--color-border-subtle). Otherwise Stack, Grid and the page archetypes from @terpjs/react-core. The bootstrap imports @terpjs/contract/tokens.css, ./house-style.css and ./theme.css.
